data.text:
Junaid Shafi Bhat vs Ut Of J&K And Others on 4 April, 2024 
Author: Rahul Bharti
Bench: Rahul Bharti
 High Court Of Jammu &Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
 Reserved on: 28.03.2024
 Pronounced on: 04.04.2024
 Wp (Crl) No. 614/2022
Junaid Shafi Bhat
 ... Petitioner/Appellant(s)
Through: Ms. Razia Amin, Advocate
 V/s
Ut of J&K and others
 ... Respondent(s)
Through: Mr. Faheem Nissar Shah, Ga
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Judgment
1.  Heard the learned Counsel for the parties. Perused the entire writ record and also the detention record. 
2. The petitioner is 24 years old young man who has come to suffer loss of his personal liberty by preventive detention custody ordered against him by the respondent No.3 - District Magistrate Anantnag vide an Order No. 49/DMA/PSA/DET/2022 dated 29/06/2022 (hereinafter to be referred in short as "the detention order") passed under the J&K Public Safety Act, 1978 on the purported ground that the petitioner's alleged activities were reckoned to be prejudicial to "the Security of the State". On account of this detention order, the petitioner came to be taken into preventive custody on 03/07/2022 and lodged in the District Jail Bhaderwah. 
3. It is against his this preventive detention which has lasted now more than one and half year in running that the petitioner through his father has approached this court with the present petition under article 226 of the Constitution of India for a writ of habeas corpus so as to regain his lost personal liberty. 
4. A case for preventive detention of the petitioner was proposed by the Senior Superintendent of Police, SSP, Anantnag who, vide his letter No. CS/71/2022/10502-506 dated 27/06/2022,
forwarded a dossier with respect to the alleged activities of the petitioner in the light of which the Junaid Shafi Bhat vs Ut Of J&K And Others on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144568715/
1 petitioner's custody under preventive detention was sought for. 
5. Drawing from the said dossier, the respondent no. 3-District Magistrate Anantnag came to set out the grounds of detention based upon which a subjective satisfaction was purportedly formed by the respondent No.3-District Magistrate Anantnag that the petitioner deserves deprivation of his personal liberty otherwise a guaranteed fundamental right of the petitioner. 
6. The grounds of detention profiled the petitioner by reference to his brother Umais Shafi Bhat who got killed in an encounter with Security Forces at Takiya Maqsood Shah Bijbehara on 23/11/2018 as he was alleged to be affiliated with terrorist organisation "HM". The petitioner is alleged to have made close contact with the banned terrorist organisation HM with an aim and intention to provide logistic support in terms of food/shelter/car transportation to terrorist from one place to another in the outskirts of Bijbehara town and also carrying out the task of keeping a close vigil on the Security Forces. With this background the petitioner was reckoned to be a risk to be let free in the wake of annual Amarnath Yatra. The petitioner was alleged to be working on the direction of militants whose aim was to disrupt the peaceful atmosphere and to secede the UT of J&K from the rest of the Country. 
7. Without any factual content worth name cited and stated by the respondent No.3-District Magistrate Anantnag, the preventive detention of the petitioner came to be granted by the respondent 3 - District Magistrate Anantnag which came to be confirmed by the Government vide a Govt. Order No. Home/PB-V/1588/2022 dated 08/08/2022.
8. Upon examining the facts and circumstances of the case, this court finds that the preventive detention of the petitioner is without any factual basis and is just based upon ipsi dixit of the SSP Anantnag and the respondent No.3-District Magistrate Anantnag . This court is left wondering as to whether the preventive detention of the petitioner is based upon application of mind or avoidance of mind on the part of the authorities above referred when just by using the cloak that the petitioner's brother Umais Bhat was affiliated with banned organisation HM before getting eliminated in an encounter, the petitioner could be given any bad profile without an iota of factual inputs. If the so called grounds of detention are to be accepted to be making a sense, then surely the petitioner would have suffered implication in some reported incidents endangering the law and order situation lest that of public disorder but without any such actual and factual input the security of the state has been reckoned to be under risk from the end of the petitioner by the respondent No.3- District Magistrate Anantnag. 
9. A seriously eroding fact with respect to the detention order passed by the respondent No.
3 -District Magistrate Anantnag against the petitioner is that the petitioner's unrevealed, undisclosed and unknown activities have been purportedly held to be prejudicial to the Security of the State whereas in the Jammu & Kashmir Public Safety Act, 1978 in terms of its section 8 there is no such ground envisaged where byreference to the Security of the State a preventive detention can be ordered. The security of the State of J&K used to be a ground for preventive detention of a person under the Act but ceased to be so w.e.f 31/03/2020 vide S.O.1229(E) of 2020 dated 31/03/2020 whereby it is now only with respect to and by reference to the Security of Union Territory of Jammu Junaid Shafi Bhat vs Ut Of J&K And Others on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144568715/
2 & Kashmir that a preventive detention can be ordered. 
10. Thus the respondent No. 3-District Magistrate Anantnag was acting without jurisdiction in ordering the preventive detention of the petitioner by reference to "the Security of the State" basis. 
11. Thus, the preventive detention of the petitioner by virtue of the impugned order dated 29/06/2022 is legally untenable and as a result whereof the petitioner's detention deserves to be quashed and is, accordingly, quashed. The petitioner is set free to his personal liberty by the Superintendent of the Jail concerned with immediate effect. 
12. Disposed of accordingly.
